subject: general
question: Privatisation of the public sector undertakings by selling off part of the equity of PSUs to the public is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Disinvestment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Disinvestment** refers to the process of selling off a portion of the government’s stake in public sector undertakings (PSUs) to private entities or the general public.
 
• The objective behind disinvestment is to reduce the financial burden on the government, improve public finances, and encourage private ownership.
 
• Disinvestment helps in improving the efficiency of PSUs as it brings in private management practices and accountability.
 
• It is also used as a tool to raise funds for specific developmental projects and to meet the fiscal deficit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalisation:**

 
 
• Globalisation refers to the process of increasing interdependence and connectivity between countries through the exchange of goods, services, information, and culture.
 
• It leads to the integration of markets, economies, and societies across the world.
 
 
 
• **Industrialisation:**
 
 
• Industrialisation is the process of transforming an economy from primarily agricultural-based to one that is based on the manufacturing of goods.
 
• It involves the development of industries and infrastructure, leading to economic growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Liberalisation:**
 
 
• Liberalisation refers to the process of eliminating or reducing government restrictions and regulations in an economy to encourage the free flow of goods, services, and capital.
 
• It aims to create a more competitive and efficient market environment.
 
 
 
• **Privatisation:**
 
 
• Privatisation is the transfer of ownership, management, and control of a public sector enterprise to the private sector.
 
• It aims to improve efficiency, reduce public sector borrowing requirements, and encourage investment and innovation.
